reconcile.note: Clarke reads Paul's eternal destruction in 2 Thessalonians as unending conscious existence under judgment rather than the extinction implied by annihilationist texts.

discrepancy.note: Ingersoll presses the same tension, quoting Christ's threat of everlasting fire against Ecclesiastes' claim that men and beasts share one common fate in death.

quotes.text: Did Christ have in his mind the shining truth that all the children of men will at last be filled with joy, when he uttered these comforting words: "Depart from me, ye cursed, into everlasting fire prepared for the devil and his angels"?
quotes.attr: Robert G. Ingersoll (d. 1899), The Christian Religion, pt. III (Ingersoll's Rejoinder to Judge Jeremiah S. Black) (1881), on Matthew 25:41.

sides.snippet: But the wicked shall perish. The enemies of Yahweh shall be like the beauty of the fields. They will vanish-- Vanish like smoke.
sides.verseText: But the wicked shall perish. The enemies of Yahweh shall be like the beauty of the fields. They will vanish-- Vanish like smoke.

sides.snippet: These will go away into eternal punishment, but the righteous into eternal life.
sides.verseText: These will go away into eternal punishment, but the righteous into eternal life.\"
